Report_ID: Incidence of radiocontrast nephropathy (RCN) at 48 hours
Title: Fenoldopam mesylate blocks reductions in renal plasma flow after radiocontrast dye infusion: A pilot trial in the prevention of contrast nephropathy
Author: Tumlin et al.
Comment: The Results text explicitly reports percentages and randomized arm totals, but it does not explicitly state integer RCN event counts. Under the verbatim-only rule, events were left null rather than back-calculated as 9 and 5. The row therefore cannot directly contribute to an event-count RR meta-analysis unless counts are verified from the original Figure 3 or another exact report. Randomized denominators were 22 control and 23 fenoldopam; no RCN-specific attrition was reported.; unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: Prospective double-blind randomized placebo-controlled parallel-group pilot trial
Study Environment: Patients undergoing coronary or peripheral contrast angiography at participating clinical centers
Medium: Intravenous fenoldopam mesylate infusion plus intravenous half-normal saline hydration
Content length: Fenoldopam begun 1 hour before contrast and continued for 4 hours afterward
Participant type: Adults with moderate to severe chronic renal insufficiency undergoing contrast angiography
Outcome measurement: RCN defined as a 0.5 mg/dL rise in serum creatinine at 48 hours or a 25% increase above baseline
Outcome variable: Incidence of radiocontrast nephropathy (RCN) at 48 hours

Title: Prospective Randomized Study of N-Acetylcysteine, Fenoldopam, and Saline for Prevention of Radiocontrast-Induced Nephropathy
Author: Allaqaband et al.
Comment: The paper does not explicitly report whole-arm RCIN event counts in Table II; it reports only percentages. Therefore event fields are left null rather than deriving counts. The displayed arm sizes (saline n=40; fenoldopam n=38) are final per-protocol analyzed sizes, not confirmed randomized denominators. Overall, 126 were enrolled and 123 completed; all three withdrawals developed hypotension due to fenoldopam, but original randomized arm totals are not explicitly reported. P=0.919 is an omnibus three-group P value and is therefore not entered as the direct fenoldopam-versus-saline comparison.; unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: Prospective randomized three-arm parallel-group clinical trial
Participant type: High-risk patients with baseline creatinine >1.6 mg/dl or estimated creatinine clearance <60 ml/min undergoing cardiovascular interventions
Outcome measurement: RCIN defined as an absolute increase in serum creatinine of at least 0.5 mg/dL within 48 hr of radiocontrast injection

Author: Cogliati et al.
Comment: The paper reports 194 randomized, but one fenoldopam-group participant was excluded after randomization after being found not to meet inclusion criteria. The AKI result therefore uses analyzed denominators of 95 and 98 (N=193), representing a departure from a fully randomized-denominator intention-to-treat analysis. Title: Fenoldopam Mesylate for the Prevention of Contrast-Induced Nephropathy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Stone et al.
Comment: Primary AKI counts use evaluable-creatinine denominators (46/137 fenoldopam and 44/146 placebo), not total randomized denominators (157 and 158). The primary endpoint could not be determined in approximately 10% of randomized patients. Report_ID: Development of acute kidney injury (reported as incidence of renal failure)
Title: Use of Fenoldopam to Control Renal Dysfunction Early After Liver Transplantation
Author: Biancofiore et al.
Comment: The reported P=.7 is the omnibus comparison across all three groups, not a direct two-arm fenoldopam-versus-placebo test. Four of 144 subjects were excluded for incomplete sample collections and 140 were analyzed; timing relative to randomization is not explicitly stated. The extracted totals are the analyzed arm Ns reported in Results/Table 1. No risk ratio was reported by the paper, so it was not entered.
domain: Perioperative nephroprotection in orthotopic liver transplantation
Study Environment: Single-center orthotopic liver transplantation and postoperative intensive care
Content length: From anesthesia induction through 96 hours postoperatively
Topic of Content: Prevention of early renal dysfunction after liver transplantation
Participant type: Orthotopic liver-transplant recipients without preoperative renal dysfunction
Recruitment source: Consecutive subjects undergoing orthotopic liver transplantation at the authors' Centre
Outcome measurement: Renal dysfunction was defined as serum creatinine levels of -1.5 mg/dl, doubling of serum creatinine within 24 hours, or acute oliguria requiring continuous renal replacement therapy
Outcome variable: Development of acute kidney injury (reported as incidence of renal failure)
additional_group_ns: Group D (dopamine 3 µg/kg/minute): n=48; 5 renal-failure events (10.4%); excluded from the planned fenoldopam-versus-placebo comparison.

Title: Effects of fenoldopam infusion in complex cardiac surgical operations: a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
Author: Ranucci et al.
Comment: Although 40 participants were randomized to each arm and the authors state that analysis was conducted according to intention to treat, two fenoldopam participants receiving preoperative chronic dialysis were explicitly excluded from renal-function and AKI analyses. Table II therefore reports 4/40 for placebo and 0/38 for fenoldopam. No risk ratio or confidence interval was reported, so none was extracted.
Design Type: Prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group clinical trial
domain: Cardiac surgery and perioperative acute kidney injury prevention
Study Environment: Single tertiary university hospital; complex cardiac operations with cardiopulmonary bypass
Content length: Fenoldopam or saline infusion begun immediately before cardiopulmonary bypass and continued for 12 hours after ICU arrival
Participant type: Adults undergoing elective complex cardiac operations with cardiopulmonary bypass
Recruitment source: Patients at IRCCS S. Donato Policlinic, Milan
Outcome measurement: AKI defined as peak postoperative creatinine greater than 2.0 mg/dL and double the baseline value, sustained for more than 24 hours within the first 72 postoperative hours
